html:
SMTO-LLM-0063 — This model server profile doesn't say where the model files are

GUID: b5d5ab6f-a3c2-54c7-aae2-c5095afd0b6f
Slug: local-ai-model-download-required
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO can't start this model server because no model files were chosen for it. SMTO never downloads a model just to start the server, so nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Download or copy the model files onto the Gateway's computer yourself, or ask the person who manages it, and note their full location. SMTO deliberately never downloads a model as part of starting the server.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the Local AI Runtime profile, put that location in model_path, and select Save. The model server can only start once the profile points to model files that are already there.
  3. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, and check whether a model server from earlier is already running. Starting again while an earlier copy is still running could create a second copy.
  4. Start the model server again in a new message that names the profile with @ (use Copy reference in Parameter Store). A task keeps the profile it started with, so only a new message picks up your saved changes.

What success looks like

  • The model server starts and its status shows ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Make sure the model finished downloading completely before you start the server.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The vLLM or llama.cpp profile has no model_path; runtime startup runs offline and never authorizes downloading model weights, so the launch was rejected before any process was created.

What this means

  • The non-Ollama launch profile has no model_path; runtime startup deliberately does not authorize fetching model weights. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The non-Ollama launch profile has no model_path; runtime startup deliberately does not authorize fetching model weights.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the accepted profile's model_path and the Gateway's local artifact inventory.

How to fix it

  • Obtain and verify the model through an explicitly authorized download or transfer to the Gateway host, then set an absolute model_path in the Local AI Runtime Parameter and start a new task with that revision. Only Ollama has a separate explicit pull_model operation.
  • Obtain and verify the model through an explicitly authorized download or transfer, then set the profile's local path.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The launch profile points to already available model files.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
